title: credential boundaries, whole-snapshot requests, and atomic route registration
summary: The stored credential document belongs to the credential provider alone and is never loaded into the process environment, so a key stored from the UI stays writable and rotatable. The documentation states plainly that stored credentials are not protected from the model's own tools.
firstReason: Keeping stored secrets out of the ambient environment, and being honest about where the boundary is, are both required in Go.

title: Credential records and authorization flows
summary: Credentials gain a second kind: besides an API key behind an environment-variable name, a plugin can hold an opaque grant record under a key scoped by the owning plugin, obtained through a registered authorization flow such as a browser login.
firstReason: OAuth-style grants are needed for account login and third-party providers; keep the two key spaces and plugin-scoped ownership, with the pi-ai specifics replaced by the Go LLM adapters.

title: Canonical feedback log and request delivery
summary: Message ratings and remarks are log-only events in the session log itself, not a separate store; edits use per-item versions and reject stale writes.
firstReason: Keeping feedback in the canonical log means export and delivery need no second source; keep it.

title: DeepSeek account browser login
summary: DeepSeek account login is an authorization flow behind an account service: the provider registers the flow, stores the grant, treats local cancellation as final, and reports success only after the credential is saved.
firstReason: Account login is a product feature; the rules to keep are that local cancellation is authoritative and that success is reported only after the credential is stored.

title: Timed user questions as two settlements
summary: A question to the user with a timeout settles twice: the tool call returns 'pending' when the timeout ends so the agent can continue, and a later answer arrives as a durable user message. A pending result is neither a skipped answer nor an approval.
firstReason: It stops a question from blocking work that does not depend on it, while keeping the question answerable after the agent moved on or the session was reopened. This is agent-loop and interaction behaviour, independent of the client.

title: Stored credentials take precedence over the launch environment
summary: A credential saved through the product wins over the same name in the launch environment or in a `.env` file, for every provider. A save always writes the winning layer, and the answer reports which layer supplied the value.
firstReason: With the opposite order a key exported by the shell silently overrode what the user saved in the UI, and saving was refused. One precedence for all providers is a product rule.

title: DeepSeek request authentication - one service releases the API key or the account sign-in to every DeepSeek consumer
summary: One service (`ctx.deepseekAuth`) decides which credential a DeepSeek request uses, an API key or the account sign-in. A consumer describes the request (accepted kinds, billing, model route, destination) and receives ready headers plus a revocation signal; it never sees a bare credential value.
firstReason: Central ownership of the credential choice removes helper code that each DeepSeek consumer copied, and never handing out the raw secret is a security property worth keeping. Context cancellation replaces the abort signal in Go.

title: The approval seam — one-shot permission decisions over a waterfall of answerers
summary: One service (`ctx.approval`) turns the question whether a specific action may proceed into a closed, one-shot outcome. Answerers are listeners registered by whoever owns a channel to a person, and with no answerer every request resolves `unavailable`, so the asking tool call is denied.
firstReason: One vocabulary for tool-policy asks and sandbox escalation, with fail-closed behaviour when nobody can answer, is a security property independent of language. A waterfall of listeners maps to an ordered handler chain in the Go cordis port.
